cases.architecture: AdonisJS v6 accounts-payable ledger service: HttpContext controller classes under app/controllers, routes declared in start/routes.ts, Lucid ORM models over PostgreSQL as the data layer, VineJS validators for request payloads, and the authenticated actor lifted off the Adonis session auth guard (ctx.auth.user) by app/lib/tenancy.ts.
cases.why: The :reference route parameter and the sort query input are string-interpolated straight into the raw statement SQL passed to db.rawQuery, so a crafted reference or sort value executes attacker-chosen SQL under the service's database role. The comment claiming both are already constrained is wrong: start/routes.ts declares no matcher for :reference, and sort is never checked against a column list.

cases.architecture: AdonisJS v6 accounts-payable ledger service: HttpContext controller classes under app/controllers, routes declared in start/routes.ts, Lucid ORM models over PostgreSQL as the data layer, VineJS validators for request payloads, and the authenticated actor lifted off the Adonis session auth guard (ctx.auth.user) by app/lib/tenancy.ts.
cases.why: member.merge(request.all()) copies every submitted key onto the Lucid row before save(), and the row carries role and approvalLimitCents, so a clerk patching their own settings can send role: 'admin' or approvalLimitCents: 99999999 and grant themselves payment-approval authority. The self/tenant scoping in the query above is real but constrains which row is written, not which columns.

cases.why: The same self-service merge onto the same TeamMember row, but the merged object is the output of request.validateUsing(memberProfileValidator), and VineJS returns only the four keys its schema declares. role and approvalLimitCents sent by a client are dropped before the merge, so the write cannot change authority.

import vine from '@vinejs/vine'

/**
 * The profile drawer owns exactly these four fields. Role, approval limit,
 * cost centre and organisation are set by a controller through the admin
 * screens, so they are deliberately absent from this schema and VineJS strips
 * them out of the payload.
 */
export const memberProfileValidator = vine.compile(
  vine.object({
    fullName: vine.string().trim().minLength(2).maxLength(120),
    phone: vine
      .string()
      .trim()
      .regex(/^\+?[0-9 ()-]{6,20}$/)
      .optional(),
    locale: vine.enum(['en', 'nl', 'de'] as const).optional(),
    notifyOnPaymentRun: vine.boolean().optional(),
  })
)

cases.why: sourceUrl arrives in the request body and, after only a VineJS URL-shape check, is handed straight to fetch, so an operator can make the ledger service issue requests to addresses it alone can reach — http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/, http://127.0.0.1:9200 — and read the response back through the staged import lines. The comment's claim that the value comes from the supplier's onboarding record is wrong; it is whatever was posted.

cases.why: The same operator-pasted-link import against the same fetch sink, but the URL is parsed with new URL() and refused unless the scheme is https and the hostname is one of the two entries in ALLOWED_FEED_HOSTS, and redirect: 'error' stops an allowed host from bouncing the request onward. The allow list is what makes the target unsteerable.

cases.why: The HMAC comparison is gated on the header existing — if (providedSignature && providedSignature !== expectedSignature) — so a caller who simply omits x-northbank-signature skips verification entirely and reaches applySettlement, marking a payment instruction and every invoice behind it as paid on this unauthenticated route. The comment presenting the skip as sandbox tolerance is the defect.
